channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar holds after weak US durable goods data
item.description: NZD/USD trades near the 0.5790 area on Monday, struggling to extend its recovery despite modest weakness in the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Hawkish MAS supports SGD against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan notes that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) delivered a second consecutive tightening by slightly increasing the Singapore Dollar (SGD) Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) slope, reinforcing SGD resilience.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Political risks temper valuation case – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports that the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) and Jakarta equities underperformed after Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo unexpectedly resigned two years before his term ends, raising concerns about political interference.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ tightening yet weaker JPY against US Dollar – BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas strategists see Japan’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth slowing to 0.8% in 2026 from 1.1% in 2025 as higher inflation and energy-related costs weigh on activity, partly offset by fiscal support and AI (Artificial intelligence) investment.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: MAS signals inflation concern – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay notes Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) unexpectedly tightened policy for a second meeting, slightly increasing the Singapore Dollar (SGD) Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) slope and stressing the move was smaller than April’s.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar softens as Oil plunges on Middle East pause
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) traded mostly unchanged on Monday as a temporary pause in hostilities between the United States and Iran reduces demand for safe-haven assets. The US Dollar Index (DXY) traded lower earlier in the session but moved closed to breakeven by the late American afternoon.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Range holds as intervention fears bite
item.description: The EUR/JPY holds firm around 163.70 on Monday as the Japanese Yen strengthens, with investors cautious about opening fresh hawkish bets amid fears of intervention in the foreign exchange market.

item.title: LatAm FX: Carry appeal faces Fed test – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu at BNY sees Latin American (LatAm) assets benefiting again from improved terms of trade for energy and soft commodity exporters, with strong real-rate anchors supporting currencies and duration.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Bulls eye 0.8200 as rally extends
item.description: The USD/CHF extends its advance for the sixth straight trading session, up 0.11%, as the Greenback holds firm against a basket of six currencies, the US Dollar Index (DXY). At the time of writing, the pair trades at 0.8190, with buyers targeting 0.8200.

item.title: Gold rises toward $4,070 as falling US yields support Bullion
item.description: Gold price registers gains of 0.58% as Washington pauses attacks on Tehran, while US President Donald Trump opened the door for a resumption in negotiations. This, along with falling US Treasury yields, is a tailwind for Bullion prices with XAU/USD approaching $4,070.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Could Fed decision trigger a break from $55-$62 range?
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) reverses part of its earlier gains on Monday as the US Dollar (USD) rebounds after opening the week with a bearish gap following a temporary pause in attacks between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: Germany: Recovery potential versus energy drag – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Jörg Krämer argues that high energy prices will continue to weigh on the German economy in the second half of 2026, limiting full-year growth to 0.6%.

item.title: Euro flat after losing early gains on Monday
item.description: EUR/USD trades lower near the 1.1370 area on Monday, surrendering earlier gains as investors remain cautious ahead of key Eurozone growth figures and the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy decision.

item.title: The Dow Jones Industrial Average buys a peace nobody has signed, and the chips take it back
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades near 52,200, up around 250 points, on Monday after a session that handed it the month's cleanest bullish catalyst and then took most of it back.

item.title: British Pound tumbles as risk-off mood boosts the US Dollar
item.description: The Pound Sterling retreats by 0.13% even though the Greenback is flat during the day.

item.title: Swiss Franc slips against the US Dollar on diverging monetary policy expectations
item.description: USD/CHF climbs to fresh highs since June 2025 on Monday after Bloomberg reported that the Swiss National Bank (SNB) could keep its policy rate at zero until the end of 2027. The SNB later declined to comment on the report, according to Reuters.

item.title: Japanese Yen firms as easing tensions weigh on USD before Fed, BoJ
item.description: USD/JPY edges lower on Monday and trades around 163.70 at the time of writing, down 0.09% on the day, as the US Dollar (USD) comes under pressure from improving risk sentiment following the latest geopolitical developments.

item.title: Gold struggles below $4,100 as US Dollar rebounds, Fed decision looms
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) opens the week with a bullish gap on Monday but struggles to build on its early advance as optimism over a temporary pause in attacks between the United States (US) and Iran fades and Oil prices recover from intraday lows.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: MAS signals inflation concern – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay notes Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) unexpectedly tightened policy for a second meeting, slightly increasing the Singapore Dollar (SGD) Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) slope and stressing the move was smaller than April’s.

item.title: Australian Dollar retreats from intraday gains ahead of Australian CPI and Fed decision
item.description: AUD/USD retreats to 0.6990 on Monday, though still up on Friday's close, after briefly rising as high as 0.7011 during the Asian session as investors prepare for key Australian inflation data and the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Technical outlook remains constructive above 1.4000
item.description: USD/CAD edges higher on Monday, paring earlier losses as the US Dollar (USD) rebounds after opening the week with a bearish gap. The Greenback initially weakened as a temporary pause in attacks between the United States (US) and Iran improved risk sentiment.

item.title: Bank of England: Higher bar seen for rate hikes - ING
item.description: ING’s James Smith expects the Bank of England to keep rates on hold on 30 July and sees a prolonged pause extending through 2026. New forecasts are likely to show UK inflation peaking near 3%, below the 4% level seen as risky.

item.title: WTI Oil drops more than 7% as US, Iran pause strikes
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil extends its decline on Monday, trading around $82.60 per barrel at the time of writing, down 7.4% on the day.

item.title: British Pound: Growth slowdown and higher rates – BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas strategists expect United Kingdom (UK) growth to slow to 1% in 2026 from 1.3% in 2025, with renewed inflation pressures from the war in Iran pushing inflation to 3.2%.

item.title: Euro: Recovery signals offer limited upside against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that Eurozone leading indicators, including Germany’s IFO, Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) and ZEW, point to improving activity.

item.title: Euro trims gains as geopolitical risks, Fed outlook support US Dollar
item.description: EUR/USD reverses its early gains on Monday and moves toward filling the bullish gap at the weekly open. The pair initially rose after a temporary pause in attacks between the United States (US) and Iran improved risk sentiment, sent Oil prices sharply lower and weighed on the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: European Central Bank: Rate path and yields after sharp rise – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists argue July’s global fixed income selloff looks stretched, especially in Western Europe where 2-year and 10-year yields have risen about 30bp in four weeks.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Mixed signals keep rates on hold – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economists Taimur Baig and Chang Wei Liang argue that sticky United States (US) inflation keeps pressure on the Federal Reserve (Fed), but soft consumption, weak investment and fading labour market resilience justify a pause in Fed Funds rate hikes.

item.title: US Dollar: Policy uncertainty supports USD – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu says softer June Consumer Price Index (CPI) has reduced immediate inflation concerns, but limited Fed guidance continues to support policy uncertainty and US Dollar (USD).

item.title: British Pound: Downside risks from softer UK data – HSBC
item.description: HSBC argues that GBP/USD faces renewed downside as UK disinflation and a softer labour market reduce urgency for further Bank of England tightening, even though markets still price hikes out to 2027.
